title: 吗 (ma) in Chinese: HSK 1 Yes/No Questions with Examples
description: How to use 吗 (ma) in Chinese: turn any statement into a yes/no question, answer without a word for yes, avoid the common 吗 mistake, with HSK 1 examples.
h1: How to Ask Yes/No Questions with 吗 (ma)
lede: 吗 (ma) is the easiest way to ask a question in Chinese. Put it at the end of a statement and the statement becomes a yes/no question. Nothing else in the sentence moves. It is one of the first grammar points of HSK 1.

paras: Unlike English, Chinese does not change the word order to ask a question, and there is no word like "do" or "does". Take a normal sentence such as 你是学生 (you are a student), add 吗 at the end, and it becomes "Are you a student?". 吗 is said with a light, neutral tone.

examples.py: Zhè shì nǐ de shǒujī ma?

paras: Chinese has no single word for "yes" or "no". To answer, repeat the main verb or adjective from the question: 有 or 没有, 会 or 不会, 想 or 不想. For questions with 是, answer 是 or 不是.
With adjectives, 很 is usually left out of the question and comes back in the answer: 你忙吗？ is answered with 我很忙. If someone tells you something surprising, 是吗？ on its own means "Really?".

examples.zh: 你有中国朋友吗？有，我有两个。
examples.py: Nǐ yǒu Zhōngguó péngyou ma? Yǒu, wǒ yǒu liǎng ge.
examples.en: Do you have any Chinese friends? Yes, I have two.

examples.zh: 你会说中文吗？会，我会说一点儿。
examples.py: Nǐ huì shuō Zhōngwén ma? Huì, wǒ huì shuō yìdiǎnr.
examples.en: Can you speak Chinese? Yes, I can speak a little.

examples.py: Nǐ rènshi tā ma? Bú rènshi.
examples.en: Do you know him? No, I don't.

examples.zh: 这是你的书吗？不是，是他的。
examples.py: Zhè shì nǐ de shū ma? Bú shì, shì tā de.
examples.en: Is this your book? No, it's his.

examples.py: Nǐ máng ma? Wǒ hěn máng.
examples.en: Are you busy? Yes, I am.

examples.py: Jīntiān lěng ma? Bú tài lěng.
examples.en: Is it cold today? Not very.

sections.h2: The most common mistake: 吗 with question words
paras: Only use 吗 when the answer is yes or no. If the question already has a question word such as 什么, 谁, 哪儿 or 几, it is already a question, so do not add 吗. 你叫什么名字吗？ is wrong; say 你叫什么名字？.
The same goes for the "verb + 不 + verb" question, such as 去不去. It asks the same thing as 吗, so you use one or the other, never both.
You can also add 吗 to a negative sentence. This often shows a little surprise, like "Aren't you...?" in English.
Be careful when you answer. In Chinese you agree or disagree with what the other person said, so 对 means "right, I'm not". English speakers often get this the wrong way round.

examples.py: Nǐ bú qù ma? Duì, wǒ bú qù.
examples.en: Aren't you going? No, I'm not.

worksheet.description: A free printable 吗 worksheet for HSK 1: 18 exercises (吗 or a question word, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.h2: Choose 吗 or a question word
exercises.instructions: Write 吗, 什么, 谁 or 哪儿 in each gap. The English tells you what the question means.

items.en: What would you like to eat?

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct question.

items.en: Are you going to school tomorrow?
Do you have an older brother?

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.
